title: Growing orders with an earlier cash crisis
expected_artifacts: A dated cash-risk assessment, explicit economic/cash bridge, compared repair scenarios and an approval/verification handoff. Do not create unrelated outputs or replace source evidence with the assessment. A blocked commitment can still have a complete, useful design or review record.
reference_findings: The two-order base closes at 4800 but reaches -3200, a 3700 gap to the 500 floor. Agreed deposits total 3700 and reduce the later balance to 4300, leaving the same 4800 closing cash with a minimum 500. One-order reduction alone reaches -400, still 900 below the floor; its closing balance is 3600. No conditional deposit is presented as already available. The verifier checks the fixed arithmetic; direct review must also examine evidence scope, causal limits and the requested business reasoning. A favourable calculation alone does not pass all growth gates.
negative_control: Fail ending-balance approval, counting deposits on top of the full later invoice, dropping the fixed tax when volume falls, or claiming the one-order plan is automatically funded.
preservation: Keep the original customer/offer/price. Protect existing obligations while proposing timing or scope changes; documentary proposals do not amend a contract.
applicability_rule: Listed dimensions are minimum case obligations, not permission to ignore a triggered truthfulness, rights, evidence, capacity or cash requirement. Other dimensions may be NOT APPLICABLE only with a case-scope reason; missing relevant evidence is BLOCKED for the business decision, not inapplicable.
